(2) Sign of τ_j in the loop identity. Source: "rot(P_ε)=rot(P)-τ_j(P) in the loop sector". Lean line 26: `rotationNumber (softInsertion P j q ε) = rotationNumber P - (turn P j : ℝ)`, a real identity with the SignType cast. Same sign (and consistent with the proof's bookkeeping at lines 359-361 where τ_j=1 gives difference -2π).

(3) Hypotheses. Generic = G1 ∧ G2 (Generic.lean 11-19) matches def:generic (G1)/(G2) verbatim. SoftAdmissible (SoftInsertionTuple.lean 65-67) is exactly the three determinant conditions of def:soft lines 1013-1014 (and implies q ≠ 0). `hn : 3 ≤ n` is the framework's standing "Let n ≥ 3" of def:polygon (sm-1 line 28), not an extra hypothesis. "ε small (lem:soft-generic)" is rendered as ∃ ε₀ > 0, ∀ ε, 0<ε→ε<ε₀→…, and the Lean additionally asserts Generic (P_ε) on that interval (stronger, not weaker; by lem:rot(ii) rot is constant on any such interval so the choice of ε₀ is immaterial).

(4) Objects. rotationNumber = (Σ_i principalTurn P i)/(2π), principalTurn P i = principalAngle (edge P (i-1)) (edge P i) = arg(conj(ℓ_{i-1})·ℓ_i), which on regular pairs lies in (-π,π) with cos = ⟨u,v⟩/(|u||v|) and sgn = sgn det (principalAngle_bounds/cos/sign) — exactly def:regular's ϑ_i and lem:rot's rot on the regular locus, where P (generic ⇒ regular, lem:g1(ii)) and P_ε (generic by the Lean's own clause) live. softInsertion is pinned to the printed family (μ_1,…,μ_j, μ_j+εq, μ_{j+1},…,μ_n): softInsertion_old/new give the vertex values, edge_softInsertion_old/soft/return give edges ℓ_k (k≠j), εq, ℓ_j-εq, and softOldIndex_attachment_next / softNewIndex_next / softOldIndex_next give the cyclic successor order; rot is shift-invariant so the relabelling is harmless.

(5) Cones. openCone u v = {a•u + b•v | a,b>0} (SoftRotation.lean 40-41); for the non-parallel consecutive edges of a generic P this is precisely the open wedge strictly between u and v of width |θ|<π. Same-sign ↔ q = a•ℓ_{j-1} + b•ℓ_j (a,b>0) = q ∈ openCone ℓ_{j-1} ℓ_j; loop ↔ q = a•(-ℓ_{j-1}) + b•(-ℓ_j) = q ∈ openCone (-ℓ_{j-1}) (-ℓ_j); mixed ↔ q ∉ closure(openCone ℓ_{j-1} ℓ_j) ∧ q ∉ closure(openCone (-ℓ_{j-1}) (-ℓ_j)), which is the complement of closure(C₁) ∪ closure(C₂) — the printed "complement of the closures of these two cones" — with the same two cones as in the previous two clauses. The equivalences are stated for the given admissible q, which is the only sensible reading since sectors are defined (lem:soft-generic) for admissible q and the open wedge contains non-admissible vectors.

adversarial_refutations.argument: After a clause-by-clause comparison I could not refute the fidelity claim. (1) Hypotheses: `hP : Generic P` unfolds to G1 ∧ G2 = def:generic (G1)/(G2) verbatim; `hq : SoftAdmissible P j q` is literally def:soft's three determinant conditions det(ℓ_{j−1},q)≠0, det(q,ℓ_j)≠0, ∀k≠j det(q,μ_k−μ_j)≠0; `hn : 3 ≤ n` is the source's standing convention (def:polygon: "Let n≥3"), not an added hypothesis; "ε small (lem:soft-generic)" is rendered as ∃ε₀>0 ∀0<ε<ε₀ with Generic(P_ε) included in the conclusion (extra content, not weaker). (2) Rotation identities: `rotationNumber = (∑ principalTurn)/(2π)` with `principalTurn P i = principalAngle (edge P (i−1)) (edge P i)` meeting PrincipalAngleSpec (θ∈(−π,π), cos θ = ⟨u,v⟩/(|u||v|), sign θ = sign det(u,v)) — exactly def:regular / lem:rot's rot(P)=(1/2π)∑ϑ_i; `turn P j = chi P (j−1) j (j+1)` = τ_j; `softAttachmentMinus/Plus = −sign det(ℓ_{j−1},q) / −sign det(q,ℓ_j)` = χ_−/χ_+ of def:soft (which the source says hold for every ε>0, so evaluating on P is right). Same-sign (χ_−=χ_+=−τ_j) ∨ mixed (χ_−≠χ_+) → rot P_ε = rot P; loop (χ_−=χ_+=τ_j) → rot P_ε = rot P − (τ_j : ℝ); sector predicates match lem:soft-generic (iv). (3) Cones, the focus: same-sign ↔ ∃a b>0, q = a•edge P (j−1) + b•edge P j is `openCone ℓ_{j−1} ℓ_j` unfolded, with edge P i = P(i+1) − P i so edge P (j−1) = μ_j − μ_{j−1} = ℓ_{j−1} and edge P j = ℓ_j — the printed cone between ℓ_{j−1} and ℓ_j; loop ↔ the same with −edge P (j−1), −edge P j — the printed cone between −ℓ_{j−1} and −ℓ_j (u,v independent since G1 gives τ_j≠0, so this is the wedge of the turn). Mixed ↔ q ∉ closure(openCone ℓ_{j−1} ℓ_j) ∧ q ∉ closure(openCone (−ℓ_{j−1}) (−ℓ_j)): "the complement of the closures of these two cones" is (cl C₁ ∪ cl C₂)ᶜ = cl C₁ᶜ ∩ cl C₂ᶜ by De Morgan, i.e. exactly the conjunction of the two non-memberships; the alternative parse cl(C₁∪C₂)ᶜ is the same set because closure commutes with finite unions. `closure` is Mathlib's topological closure on Plane := ℝ×ℝ (Euclidean topology). The iff is asserted for admissible q, which is the source's own scope (standing hypothesis "q admissible at j"); over all q∈ℝ² the printed mixed identity would be false (q = ℓ_{j−1} has χ_−=0≠χ_+ but lies in cl C₁), so the admissible reading is the only one under which the source is true, and the Lean matches it. (4) softInsertion: the characterizing lemmas softInsertion_old/new, softOldIndex_attachment_next (softOldIndex j j + 1 = softNewIndex j), softNewIndex_next, soft_indices_exhaust and edge_softInsertion_{old,soft,return} show the new vertex P j + ε•q sits immediately after μ_j with edges ℓ_{j−1}, ε•q, ℓ_j − ε•q and the rest unchanged — def:soft exactly. No printed sub-clause lacks a Lean counterpart; nothing is weaker or differently quantified. The only place the Lean could be strengthened (cone iffs need only the first two admissibility conditions, not the third) is not a discrepancy, since the source states them under full admissibility.
